title: VLANs and trunking
summary: Split two switches into VLANs and carry them over one trunk link.
objectives: Place access ports in the right VLAN
Carry several VLANs over a single trunk link
See why hosts in different VLANs cannot talk at layer 2

tasks.title: Create the VLANs
tasks.description: PC1 and PC2 belong to VLAN 10 (sales). PC3 belongs to VLAN 20 (printers). Create both VLANs on both switches.
hints: VLANs are local to a switch: each switch needs its own VLAN table entry.
Open the console of a switch and enter system view first.

tasks.title: Assign the access ports
tasks.description: Put SW1 GE0/0/1 (PC1) and SW2 GE0/0/1 (PC2) in VLAN 10, and SW2 GE0/0/2 (PC3) in VLAN 20.
hints: An access port belongs to exactly one VLAN and carries its frames without a tag.
Enter the interface, set the link type to access, then set its default VLAN.
Example: interface GE0/0/1, then port link-type access, then port default vlan 10

criteria.label: SW1 GE0/0/1 is an access port in VLAN 10
SW2 GE0/0/1 is an access port in VLAN 10
SW2 GE0/0/2 is an access port in VLAN 20

tasks.title: Configure the trunk
tasks.description: The link between the switches (GE0/0/24 on both) is parked as an access port in an unused VLAN, so it carries nothing. Make it a trunk that carries VLANs 10 and 20.
hints: A trunk keeps the VLAN tag so several VLANs can share one cable.
Both ends must be trunks, and both must allow the VLANs.
Example: port link-type trunk, then port trunk allow-pass vlan 10 20

tasks.title: Verify the result
tasks.description: PC1 and PC2 must now share a broadcast domain across the trunk, while PC3 is isolated from PC2 in its own VLAN.
hints: If PC1 and PC2 still cannot reach each other, check the VLAN on each access port and on both trunk ends.

criteria.label: PC1 reaches PC2 through the trunk
